paragraphs: I'm applying for the Summer 2027 Information Security Engineer Internship in Los Angeles. A security team whose missed vulnerabilities would touch the real world is the kind of work I want to learn, and I like that interns audit real code and build tooling that outlasts the summer. I finished my B.S. in Computer Science at UC Irvine, specializing in Networked Systems, and I'm local to Orange County.

The vulnerability classes you list are the ones I've spent the most time on. I built and still operate CommunicAI, an AI-powered iOS app on the App Store, and I own its security. I designed its role-based access-control rules specifically against authorization flaws (IDOR, privilege escalation and message spoofing), and 36 adversarial unit tests try to break them. I implemented its authentication (Sign in with Apple with nonce and SHA-256 hashing, Google OAuth and verified email/password), and its server-side Cloud Functions enforce input validation, rate limiting and receipt verification against fraud. In labs I've used Burp Suite and Wireshark to work through SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, buffer overflows, MITM, ARP poisoning and DNS spoofing, and my coursework covered RSA, ECC and TLS.

I write Python and C/C++, and I enjoy reading unfamiliar code to understand how it breaks. When the obvious attack fails, I keep going. I'm studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam in January. As captain of UC Irvine's NCAA Division I track and field team, I'm used to full days and extended effort.
I'd love to help your team find gaps before anyone else does. I'm available full-time on-site for the whole Summer 2027 internship.
